metadata.title: Helium star donor channel to type Ia supernovae and their surviving companion stars

evidence.quote: US 708 is an extremely He-rich sdO star in the halo of the Galaxy
which could be an alternative origin for hypervelocity stars (HVSs), especially for HVSs such as US 708.
hypervelocity stars (HVSs), which are stars with a velocity so great that they are able to escape the gravitational pull of the Galaxy.
Thus, a surviving companion in the He star donor channel may have a high velocity like US 708.

values.condition: Heliocentric radial velocity reported by Hirsch et al. (2005)

evidence.quote: US 708 is an extremely He-rich sdO star in the halo of the Galaxy, with a heliocentric radial velocity of +708 ± 15 km/s (Hirsch et al. 2005).

notes: US 708: T:p1-b4 treats it as an HVS, while T:p3-b1 defines HVSs as stars able to escape the Galaxy; T:p4-b1 discusses it as a possible surviving companion. It is recorded as follow_up because the paper is assessing an already known HVS rather than newly identifying it as an unbound candidate.

US 708: The paper only reports US 708's heliocentric radial velocity from Hirsch et al. (2005). The spatial velocity distribution (>400 km/s) and the ~30% fraction with observed velocity >700 km/s refer to the simulated population of surviving companions in the He star donor channel, not to US 708 individually, so they are not recorded as US 708 values.
